description: Every CortexMessageType the shipped Cortex Control binary declares, and what this stack does about it. The protocol layer decodes and encodes all of them through packages/rust/qc-protocol/src/message_registry.rs, which is generated from the same table; this file records which types the application does not drive, and why. tools/verify_cortex_protocol_message_types.py fails if a type is undecodable, if it is neither driven nor explained here, or if a type listed here starts being driven - so a newly discovered type cannot sit unexamined and a closed gap cannot linger as a stale excuse.

categories.factory: Manufacturing and production test. Reaching these from a controller is meaningless outside Neural DSP's line, and several write calibration or serialization data that must not be guessed at.
categories.cloud: Cortex Cloud account, product entitlement and download plumbing. Needs Neural DSP account credentials and a server contract that is not in the binary's descriptors; the device-side half alone is not usable.
categories.telemetry: Continuous meter, load and log streams. They report; nothing about controlling a device depends on them, and subscribing costs bandwidth on a link that already paces poorly.
categories.unestablished: Observed or declared, but the contract is not understood well enough to send safely. Recorded with what is known so it can be finished rather than forgotten.

types.name: IOMeter
types.note: Input and output level meters. The I/O screens we drive read levels from the settings replies instead.

types.name: Diagnostics
types.note: SOC2ARM comms diagnostics counters, including the four USB-audio counters newer firmware added.

types.name: CloudLogin
types.note: Its trailer flags a non-protobuf body, so even the framing differs from the rest.

types.name: CPULoad
types.note: The CPU monitor screen is reconstructed from state we already hold.

types.name: BackupsForward
types.note: Cloud backup forwarding. Local backup over type 40 is implemented and is the path a controller needs.

types.name: GridModelMeter
types.note: Per-block meter feed. Observed around block edits alongside ModelPreset; see type 71.

types.name: RecentSearches
types.note: Device-side search history. We render the search screens from the device's own scene graph and never write history back, deliberately: it is the user's data.

types.name: GigViewButton
types.note: Gig View button presses. We drive Gig View through the RemoteControl surface (type 72) instead, which is what the screen corpus is captured with.

types.name: PresetSpeedTest
types.note: Benchmark harness, not a control path.

types.name: UpdaterForward
types.note: Firmware update forwarding. ST-06 is marked do-not-trigger in the capture plan for the same reason: starting an update is not reversible.

types.name: GainCalibration
types.note: Writes calibration data. Guessing at this changes how the unit measures its own inputs.

types.name: NeuralCapture2
types.note: A second-generation capture message. The wizard we drove end to end on hardware uses NeuralCapture (42); nothing on CorOS 4.1.0 was observed using this one.
